title: Societies compared: verified targets for the money (pilot-societies-1)

design.question: For the same agents, checker and money, does OSO reach the same verified targets for less than other ways of organizing the agents?
design.compare: Single agent, Independent labs, Shared library, Planner, Traditional, OSO, α 0.8, OSO, α 0.2
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $0.60 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: money spent to verify 2 of the counted targets (C3, A3, C4, X1, B3, B5, X2, A5); a run that never does counts as its whole budget

answer: OSO, α 0.8 reached 2 verified targets for $0.03 on average, the same as Independent labs over 2 paired runs (no clear difference; ±$0.04). OSO, α 0.2 reached 2 verified targets for $0.02 on average, the same as Independent labs over 2 paired runs (OSO cheaper; ±$0.00).

table.settings: one lab, all the money · α 1, c 0
shared at once · α 1, c 0 · lab 1 assigns the work
shared when a target is proved · α 1, c 0

caveats: Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs; the verdict compares runs in pairs (run k of each society), with ± two standard errors of the difference.
